The season began on 16 February and ended on 22 December 2024.{{cite web|url=https://premiumsportsbo.com/la-temporada-empezara-el-16-de-febrero-con-un-torneo-por-series/|title=La temporada empezará el 16 de febrero con un torneo 'por series'|trans-title=The season will start on 16 February with a tournament 'by series'|publisher=Premium Sports|language=es|date=10 January 2024|access-date=10 January 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://fbf.com.bo/d-noticia.php?id=1415|title=El Consejo de la División Profesional del fútbol boliviano aprobó el Calendario 2024|trans-title=The Council of Bolivian football's División Profesional approved the 2024 Calendar|publisher=[[Bolivian Football Federation]]|language=es|date=11 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024}} [[Club Bolívar|Bolívar]] won their thirty-first league title in this season, after winning the Torneo Clausura and defeating the Torneo Apertura winners [[C.D. San Antonio Bulo Bulo|San Antonio Bulo Bulo]] 2–0 in the championship final.{{cite web|url=https://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/bolivar-es-amo-y-senor-del-futbol-boliviano_395837|title=Bolívar es amo y señor del fútbol boliviano|trans-title=Bolívar is lord and master of Bolivian football|publisher=[[El Deber]]|language=es|date=22 December 2024|access-date=22 December 2024}} [[The Strongest]] were the defending champions. ==Format== The competition format was confirmed at the session of the División Profesional's Council held on 10 January 2024, in which it was decided that two tournaments ([[Apertura and Clausura]]) would be played in the season. In the Torneo Apertura, the 16 participating teams were divided into four groups of four teams each with a round of interzonal matches between derby rivals. The top two teams of each group advanced to a knockout stage, in which teams played quarter-finals, semi-finals, and finals. Both Apertura finalists were awarded international berths, with the winners qualifying for the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]] group stage as ''Bolivia 1'' and the runners-up claiming the ''Bolivia 1'' berth for the [[2025 Copa Sudamericana]]. The Torneo Clausura was a double [[round-robin tournament|round-robin]] competition, in which the 16 teams played each other twice for a total of 30 matches, with the top team at the end of those 30 rounds being declared as the winner and qualifying for the group stage of the Copa Libertadores as ''Bolivia 2''. It was also decided that both tournament winners would play a double-legged final series at the end of the season to decide the season champions, who also earned a monetary prize of one million [[US dollar|USD]] awarded by [[CONMEBOL]].{{cite web|url=https://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/las-cinco-claves-del-futbol-boliviano-para-este-2024_353009|title=Las cinco claves del fútbol boliviano para este 2024|trans-title=The five keys of Bolivian football for this 2024|publisher=[[El Deber]]|language=es|date=10 January 2024|access-date=10 January 2024}} The remaining international berths were awarded through an aggregate table including the Torneo Apertura's first stage and the Torneo Clausura, with the bottom-placed team in this table being relegated and the team placing second-from-bottom qualifying for a two-legged relegation play-off. ==Teams== 16 teams competed in the league for the 2024 season: 14 of which took part in the 2023 Primera División, and two promoted from the 2023 [[Copa Simón Bolívar (Bolivia)|Copa Simón Bolívar]], [[GV San José]] and [[C.D. San Antonio Bulo Bulo|San Antonio Bulo Bulo]]. GV San José achieved a first-ever promotion to the top tier on 10 December 2023, after winning the title,{{cite web|url=https://futbol.unitel.bo/futbol/gv-san-jose-es-campeon-de-la-simon-bolivar-y-logra-el-ascenso-a-la-division-profesional-KK10385294|title=GV San José es campeón de la Simón Bolívar y logra el ascenso a la División Profesional|trans-title=GV San José is the champion of the Simón Bolívar and achieve promotion to the División Profesional|publisher=A Todo Deporte|work=[[Unitel Bolivia]]|language=es|date=10 December 2023|accessdate=10 December 2023}} and San Antonio also reached the first division for the first time six days later, after winning the promotion/relegation play-offs against [[Libertad Gran Mamoré F.C.|Libertad Gran Mamoré]].{{cite web|url=https://premiumsportsbo.com/san-antonio-bulo-bulo-gana-por-penales-y-asciende-a-la-division-profesional/|title=San Antonio Bulo Bulo gana por penales y asciende a la División Profesional|trans-title=San Antonio Bulo Bulo win on penalties and promote to the División Profesional|publisher=Premium Sports|language=es|date=16 December 2023|accessdate=21 December 2023}} Aside from Libertad Gran Mamoré, GV San José and San Antonio Bulo Bulo replaced [[C.D.
